**Visual observations:**
- Corn leaf (appears to be upper surface view)
- Numerous very small, scattered orange/rust-colored pustules distributed across the leaf
- Pustules are small, circular to oval, light orange to cinnamon color
- They appear densely packed and primarily on the upper leaf surface
- One larger tan/brown oval lesion visible (possibly mechanical damage)
- No brick-red coloration typical of common rust

**Reasoning:**
The small, densely packed, light orange to cinnamon-colored pustules primarily on the upper leaf surface are classic Southern rust. Common rust pustules are brick-red and appear on both upper and lower surfaces, while Southern rust is smaller, more circular, lighter orange, and predominantly on the upper surface. The density and color match Southern rust well.
